title: Speculative kernel handoff causes KV-offset miswrite and softmax magnitude drift
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
A recent performance patch added speculative prefetching and a fast-path kernel handoff between fused-attention and fallback kernels to lower tail latency. Under specific interleavings (prefill followed by immediate decode on a different kernel), we observe KV-store writes with off-by-chunk offsets. This manifests as token misalignment during decode, subtle softmax magnitude drift, and infrequent but reproducible correctness regressions (different completions compared to baseline).

Impact:
- High: customer-facing deterministic regressions in model outputs for long-context workloads (LLM chat history re-ordering).
- Reproduces on CI with a deterministic micro-reproducer; also observed in staging runs for a subset of models (6B-20B) with quantized kernels.

Reproducer:
- repo: internal/runtime/tests/kernel_handoff_repro
- command: ./run_repro --seed 1729 --context 2048 --switch-window 3
- CI job: ci/runtime/kernel-handoff-repro (failing intermittently at ~8-12% per commit on x86 GPU nodes)
- Trace: https://dashboards.redwood/runtime/traces/hand-off-2026-03-11

Evidence collected:
- Memory diffs show KV slab writes to addresses that are misaligned by one chunk (64KB) when handoff occurs within the prefetch completion window.
- Log excerpts include concurrent kernel selector decisions with timestamps within 1-3us and overlapping KV write transactions (see attached logs in PR).
- Numeric traces show softmax sums diverging by ~1e-4 after the corrupted KV write; subsequent generation diverges after ~6 tokens on average.

Initial hypothesis:
- The speculative prefetch path writes into a shared KV slab without a strict ownership/fence when the kernel selector switches to a fallback kernel mid-prefetch. The fallback kernel uses an alternate KV layout (different chunk alignment), causing miswrite. Thermal ordering + concurrent allocator reuse exacerbates the window.

Short-term mitigation applied:
- Feature toggle: disabled speculative prefetching for fallback-kernel-eligible models in staging (runtime flag: --disable-prefetch-fallback). 
- Canary: rolled toggle to 10% of staging traffic; observed no new regressions.

Proposed fixes (priority order):
1) Add atomic handoff: introduce a handoff protocol where prefetch completes with a small metadata commit (handshake token) that a kernel consumer must check before mapping writes. This requires a light-weight fence and a metadata slot per-request.
2) Normalize KV chunk layout across kernels: unify allocator chunk size and alignment in the runtime code path so different kernels share compatible offsets. This is larger but eliminates layout mismatch risk.
3) Gate speculative path with kernel-compatibility check: prefetch only if both source and potential target kernels advertise identical KV layout; otherwise fall back to conservative prefetch.
4) Unit/integration tests: extend kernel_handoff_repro to fuzz kernel switch timing and simulate allocator reuse; add an assert-mode that verifies KV checksums after each prefetch.

Trade-offs:
- Atomic handoff adds a ~0.5-1us overhead per prefetch in worst case but is bounded and avoids correctness issues.
- Layout normalization requires churn in kernel build/ABI and could delay some optimized kernels; however it simplifies future reasoning.

Rollout plan:
- Phase A (now): keep feature toggle off in production, enable in isolated canaries once PRs are merged.
- Phase B (after fix #1 merged): enable atomic handoff behind runtime flag, run stress tests and 72-hour canary.
- Phase C (fix #2 opt-in): coordinate with kernel owners to align allocators and land a follow-up.

Testing and validation:
- Add deterministic reproducer to CI; require green on 3 consecutive runs before lifting the toggle.
- Create differential-generation test harness that compares baseline outputs to runtime outputs across model sizes and quantization configs.

Artifacts / links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood/runtime/speculative-prefetch-handoff
- Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1426 (WIP, atomic handoff prototype)
- CI failure history: https://ci.redwood/runtime/jobs/hand-off-repro/history
- Monitoring dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood/runtime/kv-offset-anomalies

Next steps (owners):
- Prototype atomic handshake in PR 1426 (owner: Marco Ruiz) -> prototype + unit tests (ETA 2026-03-15).
- Add KV layout compatibility tags to kernel registry (owner: Linh Tran) -> small spec change + kernel metadata bump (ETA 2026-03-18).
- Extend CI reproducer and add checksum assertions (owner: Aisha Patel) -> ETA 2026-03-16.

Acceptance criteria for Done:
- Deterministic reproducer fails no more than baseline CI flakiness (<1% per 100 runs).
- Canary runs 72 hours with no regression signals and telemetry showing stabilized softmax sums.
- PRs merged and rollout plan executed with required QA sign-offs.
comments: 2026-03-12 - Aisha Patel: Initial bug filed after staging alert. Attached initial logs and a minimal CI reproducer. Marked as P0 due to output correctness.

2026-03-13 - Marco Ruiz: Reproduced locally using the repro script; confirmed misaligned KV write at the allocator layer. Starting prototype for atomic handshake. Opened draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1426

2026-03-13 - Linh Tran: Noted that several optimized kernels have proprietary chunk alignment assumptions. Will enumerate kernels and add compatibility tags to the registry. This will be a separate change but necessary if we don't implement layout unification.

2026-03-14 - QA (Priya Mehta): Added stress job to nightly with 10k cycles of random handoff timing. Observed reproducible failure within 2k cycles before toggle. Will re-run against branch with handshake enabled.

2026-03-14 - Marco Ruiz: Prototype pushed to PR #1426 with handshake metadata and smoke tests. Performance hit measured at ~0.7us median on our microbench; acceptable for correctness. Requesting review from runtime core and allocator owners.
